title: Phase 3: signal ingestion
description: Needs planning: the signal→tick funnel (Worker commits tick JSON via GitHub contents API, DO inbox as conflict buffer); webhook-mode Telegram with draft-tick triage and Create/Dispatch buttons; GitHub issue ingestion behind the tk label consent boundary; generic webhook sources registered in .tick/config.md; external_ref dedup everywhere; trace IDs from the front door (D20).
notes:
2026-08-19 15:30 - [human] Scope expanded 2026-08-19 by human decision: Telegram/GitHub rungs of the UC1b command vocabulary (D21) are Phase 3. See docs/design/cloud-factory.md UC1b.
2026-08-19 21:38 - [human] Scope (human question, 2026-08-19): ONE Telegram bot/chat now serves MANY projects, since one factory serves many projects. Machine routing is already unambiguous — RunRoom is per-project (idFromName(project+epic)), question ids are unique-by-registration (afj), and inline-keyboard callback data carries the question id, so a BUTTON answer always resolves exactly one question in exactly one project. Two gaps remain:

1. LEGIBILITY. kv2 routes by project on the API side (FactoryChannel.projectPath) but nothing composes the project into the Telegram message text. Two repos in one chat produce indistinguishable questions. Every gate message, report and completion must name project + epic + tick. Cheap, and it is what makes a shared chat usable at all.

2. FREE-TEXT ANSWERS ARE AMBIGUOUS, and this is a correctness issue rather than a nicety. Rules to implement, fail-closed:
   - A Telegram reply-to a specific question message resolves THAT question. Deterministic; prefer it.
   - Bare text with exactly ONE open question across all projects resolves it.
   - Bare text with TWO OR MORE open questions must REFUSE and list the candidates. Never guess: an approval carries human provenance into the verdict guard, so a wrong guess attributes the operator's approval to another project's gate.

3. UPGRADE PATH, optional: a Telegram supergroup in forum mode gives one topic per project via message_thread_id — one bot, one chat, natively separate threads, replies scoped to their topic. The rules above are what make a shared chat work WITHOUT it, so treat topics as an enhancement rather than a prerequisite.
2026-08-19 21:40 - [human] Telegram Topics mechanics (human confirmed topics are the right answer, 2026-08-19):
- 'Topics' in the UI IS 'forum' in the Bot API (is_forum on the chat). Same feature, two names — there is no separate forum object to create. The operator already runs Topics in another group, so the capability is proven on their account.
- Requires a supergroup; enabling Topics upgrades a basic group automatically. The bot must be a member; it needs can_manage_topics ONLY to create topics itself. Posting into an existing topic just needs message_thread_id on sendMessage.
- CONFIG SHAPE CHANGE: the current channel config is a private chat (operator.json has user_id == chat_id). Group + topics means a new chat_id plus a per-project message_thread_id map. Design that map as part of project enrolment, not as a fourth config surface.
- BOT PRIVACY MODE is the non-obvious trap: in groups a bot sees only commands and REPLIES TO ITS OWN MESSAGES by default, not general chatter. Recommendation: keep privacy mode ON and rely on reply-to plus inline buttons (callbacks always reach the bot regardless). Consequence: in a group the reply-to convention stops being a nicety and becomes load-bearing for free-text answers — the fail-closed rules already recorded here still apply, but the common path becomes reply-scoped and therefore unambiguous by construction. Disabling privacy mode would let the bot read every message in a group the operator also uses for other things; that is a larger surface than this needs.
- Verification when implementing: getChat on the target group and assert is_forum, and getMe/getChatMember to confirm the bot's rights, rather than assuming — the operator's account already has a working example to test against.
2026-08-19 21:41 - Who creates what — VERIFIED against the operator's live bot via the Telegram API (2026-08-19), not assumed:
  getForumTopicIconStickers -> ok:true, 112 icon stickers  (forum API is live on this bot)
  createChat                -> 404 Not Found               (no such Bot API method)

FACTORY CAN DO, per project, forever after the one-time setup:
- createForumTopic(chat_id, name, icon_color, icon_custom_emoji_id) at ENROLMENT; store the returned message_thread_id on the enrolment row (daq's enrolled-projects table is the natural home — do not add a fourth config surface).
- editForumTopic on rename; closeForumTopic / reopenForumTopic on project lifecycle.
- 112 icon stickers are available, so each project can carry a distinguishable icon — worth doing, it is what makes a sidebar of topics scannable.

HUMAN MUST DO, ONCE (~1 minute, irreducible):
- Create the supergroup — bots CANNOT (createChat does not exist).
- Enable Topics.
- Add the bot and promote it with can_manage_topics; without that right createForumTopic fails.

This is the same boundary tk channel setup telegram already walks with BotFather: the human does the interactive bits, the tool does everything mechanical afterwards. Adding the fifth repo must involve no Telegram interaction at all — enrolment creates the topic.

MECHANIC: learn the group's chat_id from the my_chat_member update fired when the bot is added, so setup waits for the operator to add it rather than asking them to find a chat id. Same shape as today's pairing flow.
VERIFY, DO NOT ASSUME: getChat -> assert is_forum; getChatMember(me) -> assert can_manage_topics; fail with an actionable message naming the missing step.
2026-08-20 12:57 - Related to the multi-project Telegram rules already recorded here: the operator asked whether two EPICS can run concurrently on one repo. Design tick onn covers it. The disambiguation rules here were written for one run per project and must be re-checked for N concurrent epics — in particular, a topic per PROJECT does not separate two epics inside that project, so the unit of a topic may need to be the epic.
